text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Runtime p95 latency breach detected for model-serving-pool v12. Auto-escalation triggered. Root metric: p95 token latency 450ms (baseline ~60ms). Potential kernel fallback + batching failure. Paging eng-oncall
sanjay (oncall): saw it — adding context: spike started at ~2768512320, coincident with the 23:00UTC rollout of rollout-id=rl-2026-03-15.
rebecca (eng-runtime): investigating kernel fallback logs now. Early sign: increased kernel-fallback-rate and steady growth in small-batch queue wait times. Could be a bad kernel selector change in the release.
adele (support): we are getting inbound CS tickets complaining "slow autocomplete" and a handful of enterprise customers reporting timeouts. No broad 5xx spike yet, mostly timeouts/long tails.
morgan (prodops): confirming, overall QPS steady but RU per-request climbed ~2.4x for that pool. Prefetch jobs also thrashing KV cache.
sanjay (oncall): is there a quick mitigation we can flip? Feature flag for new kernel selector is ff.kernel-selector.v2 and rollout-flag rl-2026-03-15 used it.
rebecca (eng-runtime): yes. We can flip kill-switch to revert selector to v1. Command: 
```
rdwctl flags set ff.kernel-selector.v2 false --env=prod --scope=pool:model-serving-pool
```
Do we want immediate flip?
morgan (prodops): suggest partial traffic cut first to observe. But customer impact is happening now — I'd vote for immediate kill-switch on pool.
adele (support): recommend immediate — we have at least 6 paying customers affected, one escalated to priority 1.
sanjay (oncall): committing to flip now, will coordinate rollback if needed. Running command.
ops-oncall: can you post runbook link for rollback steps?
rebecca (eng-runtime): runbook: https://internal/runbooks/runtime-kernel-fallback. Steps to revert are in the post-deploy section. After flag flip, we should monitor KV eviction, batch sizes, and p95.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Flag change recorded: user=sanjay action=ff.kernel-selector.v2 false target=pool:model-serving-pool time=2768512352
morgan (prodops): seeing initial drop in kernel-fallback events in logs, but still elevated. p95 down from 450ms -> 210ms in last 30s. Good signal but not back to baseline.
rebecca (eng-runtime): next suspect is the batching heuristics in the release: the new selector interacts with the batching window and causes too-small batches under median seq len. Looking at batching logs now.
adele (support): customer update: posted note to affected accounts acknowledging degraded performance and that we're actively mitigating. CS has opened a bridge for the priority customer.
sanjay (oncall): ops-oncall, please prepare planned rollback of rollout-id=rl-2026-03-15 if kill-switch doesn't hit baseline in 10m. Who will own that?
ops-oncall: I'll own the rollback. If we do rollback, expect ~2-3 minutes for traffic to stabilize per pool. Will coordinate with release engineer.
rebecca (eng-runtime): quick check: KV cache miss rate jumped from 6% -> 34% after deploy. Prefetch tasks appear to be evicting popular prefixes. Possibly changed memory layout or prefetch batch sizes.
morgan (prodops): starting a controlled restart of the prefetch workers on two nodes to relieve thrash; will do one AZ at a time.
incident-bot: :information_source: Handoff checklist updated: mitigation=flag-flip, next=rollback-if-needed, impacted_customers=6, severity=sev2 pending escalation.
sanjay (oncall): new metrics: p95 180ms, KV miss 22% — improving. Still higher than baseline but much better.
rebecca (eng-runtime): I'll open a temporary hotfix branch to revert kernel selector logic and adjust batching window. If rollback is needed, we can push the rollback patch.
adele (support): CS bridge has the customer on. They confirm improvement but still seeing intermittent slow responses. They've paused high-volume jobs.
ops-oncall: preparing rollback playbook: 
```
# rollback steps
rdwctl rollout cancel rl-2026-03-15 --env=prod
rdwctl drainslice pool:model-serving-pool slice=canary-rl-2026-03-15
rdwctl confirm-traffic-shift pool:model-serving-pool target=stable
```
Expect coordination with infra due to connection pinning.
morgan (prodops): rolling prefetch restarts completed for AZ-1. Metrics look stable there. AZ-2 next.
incident-bot: :bar_chart: p95 trend (last 10m): 60ms -> 450ms -> 210ms -> 170ms. Keep monitoring for 15m for stabilization.
sanjay (oncall): decision: keep kill-switch active, continue prefetch restarts, no full rollback yet. ops-oncall on standby to rollback in 10m if p95 > 250ms.
rebecca (eng-runtime): I'll keep working on hotfix. Need logs from nodes that still show high batching wait times. @morgan can you attach node logs for slice id slice-42 and slice-43?
morgan (prodops): attaching excerpts: 
```
[2026-03-15T23:02:10Z] slice-42 batching_wait=85ms batch_size=2 kernel_fallback=true
[2026-03-15T23:02:11Z] slice-43 prefetch_eviction=true kv_miss=0.31
```
These match the pattern.
adele (support): updating customers: "We've implemented a mitigation that is improving latency; engineering continues to monitor and will follow up within 1 hour".
sanjay (oncall): logging post-incident timeline in incident doc: https://internal/incidents/2768512345. We'll run a blameless postmortem after stabilization.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident update posted to status page draft.
ops-oncall: standing by for rollback, but for now healthy signal across 80% of traffic.
rebecca (eng-runtime): two quick action items: 1) revert kernel selector in the rollout config so future shuffles don't pick v2; 2) add guard in batching heuristics for small-batch amplification when kernel fallback detected. I'll open PRs and link.
morgan (prodops): AZ-2 prefetch restarts done. Overall p95 ~150ms, KV miss 9%. Looks close to baseline.
sanjay (oncall): closing page but staying on-call for next hour for handoff. If any customer regressions pop up, escalate to sev1.
adele (support): I'll keep CS on watch and collect any follow-ups.
incident-bot: :memo: Incident severity final: downgraded to sev3 as mitigation held; action items assigned.
rebecca (eng-runtime): noted. After-action: we'll run targeted canary with kernel-selector v2 against synthetic workloads and measure batching distribution before re-rolling.
sanjay (oncall): handoff to night team: @morgan please take ownership for monitoring window, and I'll update oncall log.
ops-oncall: acknowledged.
incident-bot: :checkered_flag: Thread closed for active paging; comments may continue. For postmortem, please add timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigation steps, and customer impact summary to incident doc."
